tests.question: How many customers live in each city? Show the city and the number of customers, only for cities with more than 10 customers.
tests.reference_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
common_wrong_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY city

tests.question: What is the average product price in cents for each category? Show the category name and the average price rounded to two decimals.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name, ROUND(AVG(p.price_cents), 2) AS avg_price_cents
       FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
       GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
common_wrong_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name, ROUND(AVG(oi.unit_price_cents), 2) AS avg_price_cents
              FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
              JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name

tests.question: How many orders were placed in each calendar year? Show the year as a four-digit text value and the number of orders.
tests.reference_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', ordered_at) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY strftime('%Y', ordered_at)
common_wrong_sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y', o.ordered_at) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders o
              JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY strftime('%Y', o.ordered_at)

tests.question: How many units were sold in total in orders with status 'delivered'? Count item quantities. Show a single value named units_sold.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi
       JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
common_wrong_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi
              JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered'

tests.question: For each supplier country, how many products do the suppliers from that country provide? Show the country and the number of products.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT s.country, COUNT(p.product_id) AS product_count FROM suppliers s
       JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY s.country
common_wrong_sql:
SELECT s.country, COUNT(DISTINCT s.supplier_id) AS product_count FROM suppliers s
              JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY s.country

tests.question: What are the maximum and the minimum product price in cents within the category 'Audio'? Show max_price_cents and min_price_cents.
tests.reference_sql:

       FROM products p JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Audio'
common_wrong_sql: SELECT MAX(price_cents) AS max_price_cents, MIN(price_cents) AS min_price_cents FROM products

       WHERE c.name = 'Smartphones' AND r.rating = 5

tests.question: For each category, show the category name and the number of its products that have never been ordered. Include categories where this number is 0.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS never_ordered_products FROM categories c
       LEFT JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
            AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id)
       GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
common_wrong_sql:
SELECT c.name AS category_name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS never_ordered_products FROM categories c
              JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
              WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id)
              GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name

tests.question: For each category, show the product with the maximum price: the category name, the product name and the price in cents.

       JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
       WHERE p.price_cents = (SELECT MAX(p2.price_cents) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id)

              JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id

tests.question: Which categories have an average product price above the average price of all products? Show the category name.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT c.name FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
       GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
       HAVING AVG(p.price_cents) > (SELECT AVG(price_cents) FROM products)
common_wrong_sql:
SELECT c.name FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
              GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name
              HAVING AVG(p.price_cents) > (SELECT MAX(price_cents) / 2 FROM products)

tests.question: Which suppliers provide more products than the average number of products per supplier? Show the supplier name and its number of products.
tests.reference_sql:
SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM suppliers s JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
       GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.name

common_wrong_sql:
SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM suppliers s JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
              GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 6
